nodes.title: 1 · YOUR PROMPTS & SEED  -  start here

widgets_values:
# How to use this workflow

**Everything you need to touch is in this green box.**

## 1 · Your prompts and seed
Use the panel to the right. Add prompts, set a seed, hit **Queue**.
Each prompt in the batch renders the whole pipeline once — six prompts
means six full renders, so start with one.

## 2 · Your character LoRAs
The two slots below. They are **not interchangeable**:

* **Your SDXL LoRa** → drives the body, pose, hands and both upscales.
* **Your ZIT LoRa** → drives the face, mouth and eyes at full resolution.
  This is the slot your character's *likeness* lives in.

Putting an SDXL LoRA in the Z-Image slot will not error. It will just
quietly fail to apply your character.

## 3 · One thing you must fill in
Open **5. Face & Mouth Detail**, find *Face Detailer Prompt*, and replace
`TRIGGER, PROMPT FOR YOUR MODEL` with your LoRA's trigger word and a short
description of your character. That node drives the single most expensive
pass in the workflow.

Put what you want **avoided** in that same box. The *negative* prompt boxes
on the face, mouth and eye passes do nothing at all — there is a note next to
them inside that box explaining why.

## While it renders
An **image selector** window opens partway through and the render **waits
for you**. Pick the image you want and it continues. That is deliberate —
it lets you reject a bad base image before paying for the detail passes.

Roughly 4 minutes and ~40 GB of VRAM per image at the shipped settings.

## Nothing to adjust in here

The seven boxes below are the pipeline, in the order they run, already tuned.
You can open one to look — you do not need to.

* **1 · Canvas & Routing** holds `Width` / `Height`. Lower them if you run out of VRAM.
* **7 · Anatomy Detail** is off. Right-click it → **Bypass** to switch it on.

## Your image

**Save Image** writes to `ComfyUI/output/Instaraw/…`.

**Before / After** shows the raw base render against the finished image, so
you can see what the detail passes actually did. It is display only —
deleting it changes nothing.

widgets_values:
## The negative prompt boxes in here are empty on purpose

The face, mouth and eye passes run on **Z-Image Turbo** (`zimage.safetensors`,
loaded on the left). Turbo models are built for speed, and the trade they make
is that **they have no negative prompt at all.**

Anything you type into a negative box on these three passes is thrown away
before the model ever sees it. Nothing is broken and nothing is ignoring you —
the words genuinely never arrive. **Leave the boxes empty.**

### Say what you *don't* want in the positive box instead

**Face Detailer Prompt** is the only thing steering this pass, so it has to
carry both halves. Turn each "not that" into a "this":

* instead of a negative `blurry` → put `sharp focus` in the positive
* instead of a negative `bad teeth` → put `clean even teeth` in the positive
* instead of a negative `extra eyes` → describe the eyes you *do* want

### Do not turn `cfg` up to make the negatives work

It looks like the fix and it is not one. `cfg` is **1** on both detailers in
here, and on the eye pass in **6. Eyes**, because 1 is the setting this model
was built for. Turning it up does not usefully switch the negative prompt back
on — that was measured, not assumed — and it runs the model outside what it was
trained to do.

If a pass gives you something you don't want, change the **positive** prompt or
your LoRA. Not `cfg`, and not the negative box.
